bullets.title: FOXA: Wolfe upgrades to Outperform, $71 PT on Roku merger synergies
bullets.body: Wolfe Research upgrades FOXA to Outperform from Peer Perform with a $71 price target (36% upside), arguing the Roku acquisition should double Fox's long-term sales growth rate by combining Roku's data with Fox's premium ad inventory. Pro forma Fox trades at 11.8x NTM unlevered FCF and 7.5x EBITDA; SOTP analysis suggests $80/share fair value including FanDuel option and Flutter stake. FOXA is down 23% from pre-announcement levels as shareholders digest the $22B deal at >3x FOXA's multiple.

bullets.title: TTD: Downgraded to Sell at Arete Research, PT $11.60
bullets.body: Arete Research downgrades The Trade Desk to Sell from Neutral with a $11.60 price target, citing agencies reducing platform spending. The downgrade was flagged across multiple sector summaries as the headline single-stock negative of the session.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Upgraded to Buy at Deutsche Bank and Rosenblatt on digital gaming/post-split optionality
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank and Rosenblatt Securities both upgraded CMCSA to Buy, citing exploration of digital gaming franchises and new entertainment opportunities post-NBCU/Sky separation. S&P Global simultaneously placed CMCSA on CreditWatch Negative, flagging stiff competition, reduced diversification, and leverage concerns post-split. JPM also flagged a CHTR mobile partnership with an undisclosed large IPO and noted a potential CMCSA breakup could trigger broadband consolidation.

bullets.title: META: Judge rejects bid to dismiss 29-state addiction lawsuit
bullets.body: A district judge rejected Meta's motion to dismiss a lawsuit filed by 29 US states alleging Facebook and Instagram are designed to addict children. This represents a meaningful legal setback for META in multi-state regulatory action and was flagged as a key negative headline for the stock.

bullets.title: AAPL +2.7%: Supreme Court to hear Epic Games app store fees appeal
bullets.body: The Supreme Court agreed to hear Apple's appeal of a civil contempt order in the Epic Games lawsuit over App Store fees and outside-purchase commissions. AAPL gained 2.7% on the news, which markets interpreted as reducing near-term downside risk from the lower court ruling.

bullets.title: BE +10%: Expands Brookfield AI infrastructure partnership to $25B
bullets.body: Bloom Energy surged ~10% after expanding its AI infrastructure partnership with Brookfield to $25B, a roughly 5x increase, to build and finance rapid power delivery for AI data centers. The announcement came alongside broader sector gains as the FTC reportedly moved to ban Chinese inverter imports, lifting solar and fuel cell stocks.

bullets.title: DDOG acquires Adaptive ML to accelerate AI/RLOps observability
bullets.body: Datadog acquired Adaptive ML, a frontier AI startup building a Reinforcement Learning Operations (RLOps) platform for enterprise agents and models. Adaptive ML will join Datadog AI Research; terms were undisclosed. The deal is designed to accelerate DDOG's investment in agentic LLM post-training for observability workloads.

bullets.title: GS TMT: SOX +88% best quarter on record; key July catalysts flagged
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs TMT desk highlights SOX's +88% Q2 return as the best quarterly performance since the index's 1994 inception and NDX's +27% as best since Q2 2020. Key July catalysts: CRWD stock split 7/2, TSMC Japan Symposium 7/3, TSLA GigaTexas update 7/7, TSM earnings 7/16, AMD Advancing AI conference 7/22-23, 10% tariff expiration 7/24, FOMC 7/29. GS desk notes e-commerce weakness (ETSY, W, UBER -4%+) while semis led by CRDO, ALAB, AMD.

bullets.title: Q2 2026 Recap: MU +242%, SNDK +258% led; Mag 7 lost $2T in June
bullets.body: Q2 2026 saw Nasdaq +21.4%, S&P +14.9%, and SOX +87.8% (best quarter since inception), driven by AI capex and tight memory supply—MU surged 241.7% and SNDK 257.9%. However, June was painful for Mag 7: MSFT -17.2%, AMZN -11.9%, META -10.9%, AAPL -7.3% as AI ROI concerns mounted and equity supply weighed. Fed funds futures now pricing ~33bp of hikes through year-end after Chair Warsh scrapped forward guidance.

bullets.title: AMZN: Faces ACCC Federal Court proceedings over unfair Prime terms
bullets.body: Australia's ACCC commenced Federal Court proceedings against Amazon over allegedly unfair Prime subscription terms. AMZN was down 0.7% on the day while the broader hyperscaler group saw dip-buying on AI toll-booth narrative, per JPM's afternoon briefing.

bullets.title: DLR -5.8%: Acquires BX stake in N. Virginia data centers for $3.5B
bullets.body: Digital Realty Trust fell 5.8% after announcing the acquisition of Blackstone's stake in three Northern Virginia data centers for $3.5B ($1.2B cash, $2.3B stock). The company expects the deal to be accretive to FFO/share in 2027-2028.

bullets.title: AI-disrupted SaaS at multi-year lows: CRM, NOW, ADBE, HUBS flagged as earnings-compounders
bullets.body: Research note highlights 12 AI-disrupted SaaS/IT names where earnings revisions are still rising despite stocks at multi-year lows, framed as call-upside opportunities. Key highlights: CRM's Agentforce ARR hit $1.2B (+205% YoY) with $63.4B RPO backlog and 50% executed on $50B buyback; HUBS Q1 revenue +23% YoY to $881M with 16% customer growth; NOW has beaten earnings 9 consecutive quarters; ADBE down 25-30% YTD despite sell-side modeling +12% growth. INTU down 34% YTD with street at +18% EPS growth for 2026.

bullets.title: JPM suspends Internet mid/small-cap coverage; TTWO removed from Focus List
bullets.body: JPMorgan suspended ratings, price targets, and estimates for Internet mid and small-cap stocks due to policy reasons. Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) was specifically removed from the Equity Analyst Focus List; prior ratings and estimates should not be relied upon.

bullets.title: NVDA/AI inference: Etched founders argue inference is next mega-market, GPUs inadequate
bullets.body: Etched co-founders (via Invest Like the Best podcast) argue inference—not training—will become one of the largest technology markets next decade, requiring purpose-built chips optimized for throughput, latency, and power efficiency rather than current GPUs. Hyperscalers building internal chips seek 'good enough' NVDA alternatives, and TSMC's engineering collaboration is flagged as a key competitive differentiator. Demand for inference will scale to billions of concurrent users requiring orders-of-magnitude more compute than currently exists.

bullets.title: HOOD flagged in Open USD stablecoin launch; KeyBanc sees mixed impact
bullets.body: Open Standard launched Open USD stablecoin with 100+ partners including Robinhood (HOOD), Coinbase, Stripe, Visa, Mastercard, Shopify, and Affirm. KeyBanc views the launch as negative for Circle (USDC share erosion) and mostly positive for Coinbase as a partner with scale offset, while HOOD's participation aligns with its crypto expansion strategy.

bullets.title: WSM web traffic strong; NKE web traffic +13% MoM acceleration in June Week 4
bullets.body: Citi's retail web traffic tracker shows June Week 4 averaged +32% YoY—the strongest reading in 12+ weeks—with WSM brands (Pottery Barn, West Elm) showing consistently strong traffic for two months. NKE accelerated to +13% from flat in May, a notable positive given ongoing brand recovery concerns.

bullets.title: MU: Relative underperformer on session despite broad semi strength
bullets.body: MU gained only +0.8% on June 30 despite the SOX index surging ~3.9% and the broader semi group leading the market. MU had already surged 241.7% in Q2, and June's +18.9% post-earnings move raised demand-destruction/memory supply concerns that may be capping near-term upside.

bullets.title: MRVL in Hedgeye top 30 momentum longs; CCL flagged as exit
bullets.body: Hedgeye's fractal math signal strength model includes MRVL as a current top-30 momentum long across both TRADE and TREND durations, while CCL is flagged as an exit candidate after being held. TXN also appears in the top 30.
